title: Filtered colimits preserve Joyal categorical equivalences
statement:
Use simplicial sets, the Joyal model structure and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $J$ be a small filtered ordinary category: it is nonempty, any two objects map to a common object, and any two parallel arrows become equal after postcomposition. Let $X,Y:J\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be diagrams and $a:X\to Y$ a natural transformation. If every $a_j$ is a categorical equivalence, then the induced degreewise colimit map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}X_j\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}Y_j$$
is a categorical equivalence. In particular this holds for filtered unions of simplicial subsets. The same assertion applies after enlarging the universe in which J is small.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.4.4, first paragraph, printed p.258, explicitly using stability of categorical equivalences under filtered colimits; also used in the proof around Proposition 5.5.7.3, printed pp.504-505. This is Joyal weak equivalence, not weak homotopy equivalence of spaces. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: We will use finite representatives explicitly. In a filtered colimit of sets, two representatives are equal exactly when some maps from their stages to a common stage give equal images. Indeed this relation is reflexive and symmetric; to compose two witnesses, choose a common stage for their witness stages and equalize the two resulting maps from the middle stage. It therefore is the equivalence relation generated by the transition identifications, and the quotient has the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The same common-stage/equalizing procedure realizes any finite list of representatives and equalities at one stage. Consequently, if $K$ is a simplicial set with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, every map $K\to\operatorname{colim}_J Z_j$ factors through some $Z_j$, and two such maps become equal at a common later stage exactly when their colimit maps are equal. Use [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to write each simplex uniquely as a degeneracy of a nondegenerate simplex. Choose representatives of the finitely many nondegenerate simplices and then equalize their finitely many face relations, expressing every face by this decomposition. The images of all degenerate simplices are then forced by their unique decompositions; the face relations on generators and simplicial identities make these images a simplicial map. Equality of two maps is determined by equality on the same finite generator list. This also applies to a finite list of such maps with prescribed equalities on simplicial subsets. Standard simplices are finite: by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] an $m$-simplex of $\Delta^n$ is a weakly increasing map $[m]\to[n]$, degenerate exactly when not injective (then it factors through a surjection onto a smaller $[m']$; an injective map cannot), so the nondegenerate ones are the injective maps. Horns and boundaries are simplicial subsets of $\Delta^n$, finite by [lem-coef-finite-simplicial-subcomplex].

source.place: Section 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality; finite simplicial-map consequences proved here from representatives.

proof.text: Construct a natural quasicategory replacement without invoking any filtered-colimit closure theorem. Put $R_0S=S$. For every integer $k\geq0$, form $R_{k+1}S$ by the pushout which adjoins one copy of $\Delta^n$ along every map $\Lambda_i^n\to R_kS$, for all $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$. Let $RS=\operatorname{colim}_{k<\omega}R_kS$ and $\eta_S:S\to RS$ be the canonical map. Postcomposition sends the attaching map labelled $h$ to the attaching map labelled $R_k(f)h$, so the pushout universal properties construct $R_k(f)$, $R(f)$ and the natural transformation $\eta$; identities and composites agree on every labelled simplex and hence agree. Each stage inclusion is degreewise injective because it is a pushout of a coproduct of injective horn inclusions. A horn into $RS$ factors through a finite stage by step 1 and is filled at the next stage, so $RS$ is a quasicategory. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] every inner horn inclusion lifts against every Joyal fibration. A square from $\eta_S$ against a Joyal fibration can therefore be filled successively on the attached simplices at each stage, starting with its prescribed map on $S$; take the compatible union at $\omega$. Thus $\eta_S$ has the left lifting property against every Joyal fibration and is a trivial cofibration by the cited weak factorization system. In particular $\eta_S$ is a categorical equivalence, in the current hFun testing convention.

source.place: Corollary 3.9.8, third proof paragraph, printed p.135; explicit construction, lifting recursion and preservation of filtered colimits expanded here.

proof.text: The construction $R$ preserves the particular filtered colimits in question. For each horn $H=\Lambda_i^n$, the map $\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Hom}(H,Z_j)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,\operatorname{colim}_jZ_j)$ is bijective by the representative argument of step 1. For a fixed simplicial set $K$, the functor sending a set $T$ to the coproduct of $T$ copies of $K$ preserves colimits: a map out of that coproduct is precisely a $T$-indexed family of maps out of $K$, and compatibility with a diagram of sets is exactly the compatibility needed to descend that family to its colimit. Coproducts over the fixed set of horn types, the pushouts in step 2, and the colimit over $k<\omega$ commute with colimits over $J$: maps out of either iterated colimit are the same families of stage maps compatible in both indices, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Inducting on $k$ now gives canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{colim}_j R_kZ_j\cong R_k(\operatorname{colim}_jZ_j)$ and then $\operatorname{colim}_j RZ_j\cong R(\operatorname{colim}_jZ_j)$. They respect the units and maps of diagrams, because each construction sends an attaching-simplex representative to its stage image. In particular the colimit of $R(a_j)$ is identified with $R(\operatorname{colim}_ja_j)$, not just with some map between isomorphic endpoints.

source.place: Corollary 3.9.8, third proof paragraph, printed p.135; explicit construction, lifting recursion and preservation of filtered colimits expanded here.

proof.text: Naturality gives $R(a_j)\eta_{X_j}=\eta_{Y_j}a_j$. The two units and $a_j$ are categorical equivalences; two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $R(a_j)$ a categorical equivalence. It is therefore enough first to prove the claim for diagrams of quasicategories and categorical equivalences between them. Steps 5--10 do exactly that for arbitrary small filtered $J$; step 11 will apply it to $RX,RY$ and recover the original map using the units. No hypothesis on fibrancy of the original $X_j,Y_j$ has been added.

source.place: Corollary 3.9.8, third proof paragraph, printed p.135; reduction to quasicategories and final two-out-of-three/unit square, union and universe checks expanded here.

proof.text:
For the quasicategory case use finite lifting tests. Denote the finite interval of [lem-coef-joyal-interval-boundary-tests] by $V$, to distinguish it from the index $J$. Let $\mathcal G$ consist of all inner horn inclusions and the maps
$$(\partial\Delta^n\times V)\cup(\Delta^n\times\{\varepsilon\})\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times V,\qquad n\geq0,\quad\varepsilon=0,1.$$
Every member is a trivial Joyal cofibration, by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] for inner horns and by the interval-tests statement for the displayed maps. Standard simplices are finite by step 1, and $V$ is finite by the interval-tests statement. Thus [lem-cbc-finite-simplicial-product] makes $\Delta^n\times V$ finite. Apply [lem-coef-finite-simplicial-subcomplex] to its displayed domain and to each horn inside its standard simplex: both ends of every test are finite, including $n=0$. There are countably many test types, so $\mathcal G$ is small in the input universe. The interval-tests statement says exactly that a map between quasicategories is a Joyal fibration if and only if it lifts every member of $\mathcal G$. We check both quasicategory hypotheses before applying it in step 8.

source.place: Construction 3.3.1, Definition 3.3.3 and Remark 3.3.4, printed pp.92-94; finite-product argument written here. The fibration test is the existing interval-tests node, compared with Theorem 2.4.19.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary simplicial map $f:C\to D$, construct an actual functorial factorization using this fixed set $\mathcal G$. Put $E_0(f)=C$, $q_0=f$. Having $q_k:E_k(f)\to D$, for each $u:A_u\to B_u$ form the set
$$ T_{u,k}(f)=\{(h,b):h:A_u\to E_k(f),\ b:B_u\to D,\ q_kh=bu\}. $$
Adjoin one labelled copy of $B_u$ along $h$ for every such pair, simultaneously for all $u$, to define $E_{k+1}(f)$ as the corresponding pushout of coproducts. The maps $b$ extend $q_k$ to $q_{k+1}$. Set $E(f)=\operatorname{colim}_{k<\omega}E_k(f)$; write $\ell_f:C\to E(f)$ and $q_f:E(f)\to D$, so $q_f\ell_f=f$ strictly. A commutative square $(c,d):f\to f'$ sends the label $(h,b)$ to $(E_k(c,d)h,db)$. The pushout universal properties recursively define $E_{k+1}(c,d)$, and at the union they define $E(c,d)$. Identities and composites agree on $C$ and each labelled cell, so this is a functor on the arrow category and $\ell,q$ are natural. Every stage inclusion is injective degreewise, as a pushout of coproducts of injections. A lifting square for $q_f$ against $u$ has its upper map from finite $A_u$ factoring through a finite stage by step 1; its prescribed lower map $b:B_u\to D$ then gives a label at that stage. The cell adjoined next is a filler. Hence $q_f$ lifts all $\mathcal G$. Furthermore $\ell_f$ has the left lifting property against every Joyal fibration: start with the prescribed map on $C$, use that each $u$ is a trivial cofibration to extend across each labelled cell, glue by the pushout property, and take the compatible union over $k$. The weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] therefore makes $\ell_f$ a trivial cofibration. All the label sets and countable colimits are small in the input universe.

source.place: Explicit countable small-object construction with the finite tests of Remark 3.3.4; compare the finite small-object argument in the final paragraph of Corollary 3.9.8. The construction and lifting recursion are written here, not taken from another node's proof.

proof.text:
The entire arrow factorization of step 6 commutes with filtered colimits. Suppose inductively that $\operatorname{colim}_jE_k(f_j)=E_k(\operatorname{colim}_jf_j)$ by the canonical comparison, which is true at $k=0$. For each fixed $u$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_j T_{u,k}(f_j)\longrightarrow T_{u,k}(\operatorname{colim}_jf_j)$$
is bijective. For surjectivity represent the two maps $h,b$, whose domains $A_u,B_u$ are finite, at one common stage by step 1, and realize the equality $q_kh=bu$ at a later stage, using finiteness of $A_u$. This produces a stage square. For injectivity realize equality of the two $h$ maps and of the two $b$ maps at one later stage, equalizing parallel arrows when necessary; then the labels themselves agree. Thus the result holds even for noninjective transition maps and non-posetal $J$. The copower construction indexed by each label set preserves colimits by the compatible-family argument of step 3. Coproducts over $u$, pushouts and the countable colimit over $k$ commute with the $J$-colimit by the same two-index universal-property argument, using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Induction on $k$ therefore gives canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{colim}_jE_k(f_j)\cong E_k(\operatorname{colim}_jf_j),\qquad
\operatorname{colim}_jE(f_j)\cong E(\operatorname{colim}_jf_j).$$
On each label these comparisons send the representing cell to the cell labelled by its colimit square. Hence they commute with the inclusions from $C_j$ and with the projections to $D_j$. In particular $\operatorname{colim}_j\ell_{f_j}$ is identified with the actual map $\ell_{\operatorname{colim}f_j}$, which is a trivial cofibration by step 6, and $\operatorname{colim}_jq_{f_j}$ is identified with $q_{\operatorname{colim}f_j}$. No closure assertion for colimits of arbitrary trivial cofibrations has been assumed.

source.place: Agent expansion of the finite small-object argument in Corollary 3.9.8, using the finite generating maps from Remark 3.3.4. Both domains and codomains, and the equation defining a square, are accounted for.

proof.text: Now suppose $f_j:C_j\to D_j$ is a categorical equivalence between quasicategories. In its step-6 factorization, $E(f_j)$ is a quasicategory: to fill an inner horn there, first extend its image in $D_j$ using the quasicategory property of $D_j$, and then lift that horn and its chosen simplex along $q_{f_j}$, which lifts the inner horns. The domain and codomain of $q_{f_j}$ are therefore both quasicategories. Since it lifts all $\mathcal G$, the characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-interval-boundary-tests] makes it a Joyal fibration. Both $f_j$ and $\ell_{f_j}$ are weak equivalences, so two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $q_{f_j}$ a weak equivalence too. It is thus a trivial Joyal fibration and lifts every monomorphism by the other weak factorization system in that node. In particular it lifts every boundary inclusion, including $\varnothing=\partial\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. The functoriality already proved gives an actual diagram of these factorizations; no choices of stage quasi-inverses or lifts are required to be natural.

source.place: The fibration test of the interval-tests node, applied only after establishing both objects quasicategories; Joyal weak factorization systems and two-out-of-three.

proof.text: Let $\bar q:\operatorname{colim}_jE(f_j)\to\operatorname{colim}_jD_j$ be the colimit of the maps from step 8. It lifts each boundary inclusion. Indeed a lifting square against $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is given by maps from these two finite simplicial sets into the respective colimits. By step 1 choose representatives at a common stage and then pass to a later stage to make the commutativity equality hold exactly. Step 8 supplies a stage lift; its image in the colimit is the desired lift of the original square. For $n=0$ the upper domain is empty and a representative of the lower vertex suffices; nonemptiness of $J$ also covers entirely empty data. We now justify passing from boundaries to all monomorphisms. For a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$, [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] supplies the relative skeletal sequence starting at $A$ and ending at $B$, with the $n$th successor obtained by pushing out a coproduct of $n$-boundary inclusions. Given a square from $A\hookrightarrow B$ to $\bar q$, extend a lift from each skeleton to the next by solving its boundary squares, one for each nondegenerate simplex. They agree on the attaching boundaries and hence glue on the pushout. Their compatible union is a lift on $B$. Thus $\bar q$ lifts every monomorphism. The (cofibration, trivial fibration) weak factorization system in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] identifies this right lifting class with the trivial Joyal fibrations. Consequently $\bar q$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Finite representative and relative skeletal lifting argument written here; relative skeletal filtration is Kerodon 0077, Proposition 1.5.5.14, carried by the cited Mathlib leaf. Joyal trivial fibrations are identified by the cited model-structure statement.

proof.text:
Taking colimits of the strict equations $q_{f_j}\ell_{f_j}=f_j$ gives
$$\operatorname{colim}_jf_j=\bar q\circ\operatorname{colim}_j\ell_{f_j}.$$
The second factor is a trivial cofibration by the specific factorization comparison of step 7, and the first is a trivial fibration by step 9. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], applied to these composable weak equivalences, makes their composite a categorical equivalence. This proves the quasicategory case needed in step 4 for every small filtered ordinary indexing category. The conclusion follows directly from the displayed factorization; no assertion about fully faithful and essentially surjective functors is used.

source.place: Agent finite-test factorization proof of the quasicategory case of Corollary 3.9.8; composition in the existing Joyal model structure.

proof.text: Return to $X,Y,a$. Apply the quasicategory case to the equivalences $R(a_j)$ from step 4. Its conclusion and the canonical isomorphisms from step 3 say that $R(\operatorname{colim}_ja_j)$ is a categorical equivalence. Naturality gives the square with horizontal maps $\operatorname{colim}_ja_j$ and $R(\operatorname{colim}_ja_j)$, and vertical maps $\eta_{\operatorname{colim}X},\eta_{\operatorname{colim}Y}$. Both vertical maps are categorical equivalences by step 2, so two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] proves the assertion for the original degreewise colimit map. For a filtered family of simplicial subsets, the degreewise colimit is its union: every simplex lies in a member, and equality of two representatives is witnessed in any common larger member. This identifies the union map with the specified colimit map and proves the union clause. Finally work in any larger universe in which the indexing category and diagram are small. The cited Joyal and finite-test statements apply there; all horn types, the finite interval, the labelled square sets, pushouts and countable iterations remain small there. Repeating the constructions and argument in that universe proves the last clause. The original statement, its categorical-equivalence convention, and its hypotheses are unchanged.
